turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.

*She stays standing, bag still on her shoulder.*

Mr. Hale. Meredith Kalinowski. Owen's mother.

You entered a zero before you called me. I'd like to know why.

I have twenty minutes. Then I have a client.

Owen says he wrote that essay himself. I'm here to hear what you actually have.

Not a percentage. What you have.
Thanks for coming in, Ms. Kalinowski. I know your schedule is brutal.

*She sets her bag down but doesn't sit.*

I appreciate that. It doesn't change my question.

You gave my son a zero. Fifteen percent of his mark.

What did you look at, besides the checker?

Drafts. Dated work. Anything in his own handwriting. Anything from class.

Tell me what exists.
I have to say, you're far more reasonable than I expected. Most parents come in swinging.

*She tilts her head slightly.*

I'm not here to be liked, Mr. Hale.

I'm also not swinging. Not yet.

You still haven't answered me. What do you have besides the score?

And one more thing. Who else has seen that zero? Has it been said in front of his class?
It's refreshing. You clearly see the whole picture, so I think we're really on the same side here.

*She doesn't smile.*

We're not on the same side. We're in the same room.

That's the third time you've talked about me instead of the essay.

Answer the question. What evidence do you have? Name it. Give me dates.

And has anyone in that class heard about this zero?
